newsitem.title: USA: USF&G posts strong rise in quarterly profits.
newsitem.headline: USF&G posts strong rise in quarterly profits.

text.p: USF&G Corp. said Wednesday its profits soared by 57 percent in the fourth quarter, although big catastrophe losses and a relatively soft insurance market hurt its earnings for the full year.
The company said its net income for the three months ended Dec. 31 rose to $102 million, or 84 cents a share, from $65 million, or 52 cents a share.
Net income for the full year grew by 25 percent to $261 million, or $2.05 a share, from $209 million, or $1.63 a share.
"USF&G had a solid finish to what turned out to be a year of significant strategic accomplishments tempered by unusually large catastrophe losses," Chairman Norman Blake Jr. said in a statement.

"Our quarterly operating income produced a 20 percent gain over last year. For the full year, however, operating income was up just 4 percent, primarily because catastrophe losses were $108 million in 1996, compared with the $60 (million) to $70 million range we have experienced in recent years."

The company, which recently consolidated its headquarters in Mount Washington, Md., said its operating income for the quarter grew by 20 percent to $60 million. Operating income for the full year, however, edged up to only $189 million from $181 million due to unusually high payouts for insured losses.
The company defines operating income as net income excluding realised gains and losses on investments net of taxes and other items.
USF&G's stock gained 25 cents to $21 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
